scenes.visual: Dark navy canvas carrying the exact colour map from the first film: presenting-cell membrane above, T-cell membrane below, steel-blue TCR and teal partner tails faintly glowing. Bold white title centered: 'Signal Two and Two Brakes'. Schematic.

scenes.tts: In the first film, two phosphates on partner tails switched the receptor on. Those receptors vary almost at random, so some recognise our own peptides. What stops an armed T cell from attacking healthy tissue?
scenes.caption: In the first film, two phosphates on partner tails switched the receptor on. Those receptors vary almost at random, so some recognise our own peptides. What stops an armed T cell from attacking healthy tissue?
scenes.visual: Same synapse colour map: slate MHC with warm-white peptide above, steel-blue TCR with teal partner tails and bright gold paired phosphates below. Several TCR tips briefly cycle shapes to suggest random diversity, then one locks onto a 'self peptide' badge while a caution pulse glows around the T cell. Schematic.
scenes.narration: In the first film, two phosphates on partner tails switched the receptor on. Those receptors vary almost at random, so some recognise our own peptides. What stops an armed T cell from attacking healthy tissue?

scenes.tts: A fresh T cell does not trust signal one alone. Without a second cue, cultured T cells fall into anergy, a lasting unresponsive state. Full activation needs C D twenty eight to grip B seven. Presenting cells raise B seven when they sense infection.
scenes.caption: A fresh T cell does not trust signal one alone. Without a second cue, cultured T cells fall into anergy, a lasting unresponsive state. Full activation needs CD28 to grip B7. Presenting cells raise B7 when they sense infection.
scenes.visual: Split-state transition on the same synapse. First, blue TCR binds peptide-MHC while green CD28 beside it finds an empty top membrane; the T-cell glow dims to flat grey labelled 'anergy (cultured cells)'. Next, bright emerald B7 rises on the presenting cell; green CD28 locks onto emerald B7, gold phosphates flash on CD28's tail, and the T cell lights up brightly ('full activation').
scenes.narration: A fresh T cell does not trust signal one alone. Without a second cue, cultured T cells fall into anergy, a lasting unresponsive state. Full activation needs CD28 to grip B7. Presenting cells raise B7 when they sense infection.

scenes.tts: Once activated, the T cell puts up C T L A four. It resembles C D twenty eight and binds the same B seven. But it is a brake. Each C T L A four dimer grips two B seven at once, about ten times more tightly. So C D twenty eight is left empty, and it even drags B seven away to be destroyed.
scenes.visual: Beside green CD28 on the T cell, a crimson dimer labelled 'CTLA-4' rises and bridges two emerald B7 proteins on the presenting cell (badge: 'about 10x tighter in solution, schematic'). Green CD28 reaches toward an empty patch with a dotted line and its gold tail phosphates fade. Then crimson CTLA-4 yanks emerald B7 downward into an endosome inside the T cell.
scenes.caption: Once activated, the T cell puts up CTLA-4. It resembles CD28 and binds the same B7. But it is a brake. Each CTLA-4 dimer grips two B7 at once, about ten times more tightly. So CD28 is left empty, and it even drags B7 away to be destroyed.
scenes.narration: Once activated, the T cell puts up CTLA-4. It resembles CD28 and binds the same B7. But it is a brake. Each CTLA-4 dimer grips two B7 at once, about ten times more tightly. So CD28 is left empty, and it even drags B7 away to be destroyed.

scenes.tts: A second brake, P D one, works from inside. Many healthy cells and many tumours display P D L one. When P D L one binds, two phosphates appear on P D one's own tail. They call in S H P two, an enzyme that strips phosphates off proteins. So does it strip the two phosphates that called it in?
scenes.visual: The top cell shifts to a labelled 'tissue or tumour cell' displaying plum PD-L1. On the T cell, magenta PD-1 meets plum PD-L1 and two gold phosphates appear on PD-1's tail (label: 'ITSM tail'). Burnt-orange SHP-2 rises toward them. Question banner at top: 'SHP-2 strips phosphates. Does it strip these two?'
scenes.caption: A second brake, PD-1, works from inside. Many healthy cells and many tumours display PD-L1. When PD-L1 binds, two phosphates appear on PD-1's own tail. They call in SHP-2, an enzyme that strips phosphates off proteins. So does it strip the two phosphates that called it in?
scenes.narration: A second brake, PD-1, works from inside. Many healthy cells and many tumours display PD-L1. When PD-L1 binds, two phosphates appear on PD-1's own tail. They call in SHP-2, an enzyme that strips phosphates off proteins. So does it strip the two phosphates that called it in?

scenes.visual: Hold with burnt-orange SHP-2 poised below the two gold phosphates on magenta PD-1's tail and the banner 'SHP-2 strips phosphates. Does it strip these two?' readable at top. A quiet 4.5-second timer bar glides smoothly across the bottom.

scenes.tts: No, because those two phosphates are its anchor. S H P two grips both with two S H two domains, so it stays docked. Its working end then swings sideways and erases activating phosphates on C D twenty eight and partner tails. So this brake dims the cell from inside.
scenes.visual: Burnt-orange SHP-2 clamps onto both gold phosphates on PD-1's tail with two visible SH2 grips; those two stay bright gold throughout (label: 'docking site, not the target'). Its catalytic end swings sideways and wipes gold phosphates off nearby green CD28 and teal partner tails, which dim to grey. Small side panel recalls crimson CTLA-4 outside.
scenes.caption: No, because those two phosphates are its anchor. SHP-2 grips both with two SH2 domains, so it stays docked. Its working end then swings sideways and erases activating phosphates on CD28 and partner tails. So this brake dims the cell from inside.
scenes.narration: No, because those two phosphates are its anchor. SHP-2 grips both with two SH2 domains, so it stays docked. Its working end then swings sideways and erases activating phosphates on CD28 and partner tails. So this brake dims the cell from inside.

scenes.tts: Here is the second core rule. Full activation needs a second signal, and checkpoints brake outside or inside. A checkpoint is just a brake a T cell must get past. Blocking antibodies cap C T L A four or P D one on the patient's T cells. Tumour-recognising T cells keep firing, though healthy tissue can inflame.
scenes.visual: Cyan Y-shaped antibodies swoop in and cap both crimson CTLA-4 (left) and magenta PD-1 (right) on the T cell—never touching the tumour cell directly. Burnt-orange SHP-2 detaches, gold activating phosphates return, and the T cell flares back to active attack while an amber caution badge reads 'risk: autoimmune inflammation'.
scenes.caption: Here is the second core rule. Full activation needs a second signal, and checkpoints brake outside or inside. A checkpoint is just a brake a T cell must get past. Blocking antibodies cap CTLA-4 or PD-1 on the patient's T cells. Tumour-recognising T cells keep firing, though healthy tissue can inflame.
scenes.narration: Here is the second core rule. Full activation needs a second signal, and checkpoints brake outside or inside. A checkpoint is just a brake a T cell must get past. Blocking antibodies cap CTLA-4 or PD-1 on the patient's T cells. Tumour-recognising T cells keep firing, though healthy tissue can inflame.

scenes.tts: Blocking a brake helps only if T cells already recognise the tumour. Otherwise, engineers build a chimeric antigen receptor, or C A R. An antibody tip outside is fused to the zeta tail inside. It grips surface proteins directly, so no M H C is needed.
scenes.caption: Blocking a brake helps only if T cells already recognise the tumour. Otherwise, engineers build a chimeric antigen receptor, or CAR. An antibody tip outside is fused to the zeta tail inside. It grips surface proteins directly, so no MHC is needed.
scenes.visual: On the right of the same T-cell membrane, a single synthetic chain assembles: a bright white-cyan antibody fragment outside grips a tumour surface protein directly (compact label: 'no MHC needed'), linked across the membrane to a teal zeta tail with three hollow gold ITAM rings ('signal 1').
scenes.narration: Blocking a brake helps only if T cells already recognise the tumour. Otherwise, engineers build a chimeric antigen receptor, or CAR. An antibody tip outside is fused to the zeta tail inside. It grips surface proteins directly, so no MHC is needed.

scenes.tts: Yet a zeta tail alone gives signal one without signal two. Those early cells often failed to persist in patients. Engineers spliced C D twenty eight or four one B B inside. One binding event now supplies both signals.
scenes.caption: Yet a zeta tail alone gives signal one without signal two. Those early cells often failed to persist in patients. Engineers spliced CD28 or 4-1BB inside. One binding event now supplies both signals.
scenes.visual: The zeta-only CAR briefly flashes gold then fades dim ('signal 1 only — poor persistence'). Next, a green CD28 or 4-1BB cytoplasmic block slides smoothly into the same chain above the teal zeta tail ('signal 1 + signal 2'); both light bright gold and the T cell divides smoothly into active daughter cells.
scenes.narration: Yet a zeta tail alone gives signal one without signal two. Those early cells often failed to persist in patients. Engineers spliced CD28 or 4-1BB inside. One binding event now supplies both signals.

scenes.tts: That domain lets engineered T cells last. From natural checkpoints to synthetic receptors, the same wiring rules the response.
scenes.caption: That domain lets engineered T cells last. From natural checkpoints to synthetic receptors, the same wiring rules the response.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls smoothly back to show the unified synapse schematic: TCR + CD28–B7, crimson CTLA-4 outside, magenta PD-1/SHP-2 inside, cyan checkpoint antibody, and the two-signal CAR side by side.
scenes.narration: That domain lets engineered T cells last. From natural checkpoints to synthetic receptors, the same wiring rules the response.

scenes.visual: Canvas softens into dark navy. One clean centered line fades in at large high-contrast white type: 'Full activation needs a second signal, and checkpoints brake outside or inside.'
